title: Search query sequences against a target sequence database
source_kind: documented CLI workflow and shell workflow

sources.locator: Getting started > Search
createdb, SEARCH_MODULE, convertalis workflow stages

scientific_use: Find sequence similarities between query and target sets, optionally using a precomputed target index or GPU search, and emit tabular alignment results with selectable fields. The README notes that easy-search computes identity as identical residues divided by alignment length, whereas search estimates identity by default.
tool_role_basis: The source composes MMseqs2 createdb, search module, and convertalis operations; the scientific activity is applying the existing search suite.
inputs: Query and target FASTA/FASTQ files or MMseqs2 sequence databases; optional precomputed target index; sequence similarity/sensitivity and output-field settings.
outputs: Tabular alignment results (example .m8); optional taxonomy report when target taxonomy is configured; intermediate MMseqs2 result database.
dependencies: MMseqs2 binary and temporary storage; target database/index must fit available resources or be split; GPU support and compatible hardware are optional.
evidence: README Getting started > Search: easy-search examples, optional createindex, databases workflow Swiss-Prot example, sensitivity and output columns, identity caveat; data/workflow/easysearch.sh conversion and optional taxonomyreport stages.
limitations: Example FASTA contents and provenance were not inspected; resource use depends on sequence volume and indexing. The referenced Swiss-Prot reference is named, but release/version and terms were not established.

title: Cluster protein or other sequence sets and export representatives
source_kind: documented CLI workflow and shell workflow

sources.locator: Getting started > Cluster
createdb, CLUSTER_MODULE, createtsv, result2repseq and result2flat stages

scientific_use: Cluster FASTA/FASTQ entries using the cascaded clustering workflow (or the separately mentioned easy-linclust workflow whose runtime scales linearly with input size); tune sequence identity and coverage criteria and export cluster membership, representative sequences and all cluster sequences.
tool_role_basis: The workflow invokes existing MMseqs2 database creation, clustering, cluster-table, representative extraction and flattening commands.
inputs: FASTA/FASTQ sequence set; selected clustering workflow and identity/coverage criteria (README example uses min-seq-id 0.5, coverage 0.8, cov-mode 1).
outputs: Cluster membership TSV, representative FASTA, all-sequences-per-cluster FASTA.
dependencies: MMseqs2 binary and temporary disk space; memory use scales with total sequence residues and algorithm/database mode.
evidence: README Getting started > Cluster: example invocation and clustering criteria note; data/workflow/easycluster.sh stages for membership and FASTA outputs.
limitations: No clustering was run. The two algorithms answer similar redundancy-reduction needs but differ in scalability/algorithm; easy-linclust implementation was not inspected. Example DB.fasta appears as an input example but its sequence content and provenance were not inspected.

title: Assign taxonomy to query sequences by LCA of reference hits
source_kind: documented CLI workflow and shell workflow

sources.locator: Getting started > Taxonomy
taxonomy, createtsv, taxonomyreport, swapresults and convertalis stages
NCBI taxdump and UniProt accession-to-taxid mapping setup

scientific_use: Search query sequences against a taxonomy-annotated reference and assign taxonomic labels using selected representative aligned hits and their lowest common ancestor; generate LCA TSV, taxonomy report, top-hit report and top-hit alignments. README describes default LCA mode and alternative supported sources including BLAST, SILVA and custom taxonomy mappings.
tool_role_basis: The workflow composes existing search/taxonomy/database commands and supports applying sequence-based taxonomy assignment to input data.
inputs: Query FASTA/FASTQ or sequence database; target sequence database with taxonomy annotation; taxonomy tree and accession-to-taxid mapping or supported preannotated target database; LCA mode.
outputs: Per-query LCA TSV, aggregate taxonomy report, top-hit report and top-hit alignments.
dependencies: MMseqs2; target database preparation may use NCBI taxdump and a UniProt ID mapping file; network/download utilities are used by the setup script when configured to download.
evidence: README Getting started > Taxonomy describes createdb, createtaxdb, createindex and easy-taxonomy and names supported database sources; easytaxonomy.sh shows result/report outputs; createtaxdb.sh identifies NCBI taxdump files and UniProt idmapping source.
limitations: No actual classification or database preparation was executed. NCBI and UniProt source records have no pinned release or inspected terms; accuracy depends on reference taxonomic coverage and chosen LCA parameters.

title: Identify reciprocal best-hit sequence pairs

sources.locator: bidirectional search, best-hit filtering, swap/merge/sort and result2rbh stages
Supported search modes > Reciprocal best hits search

scientific_use: Compare two sequence databases in both directions, select each sequence's best hit, and report reciprocal pairs. This supports candidate orthology or cross-dataset correspondence analyses, but the workflow itself establishes reciprocal similarity rather than biological orthology.
tool_role_basis: The workflow composes existing MMseqs2 search, filterdb, swapresults, mergedbs and result2rbh operations.
inputs: Two MMseqs2 sequence databases and separately chosen search parameters for A-vs-B and B-vs-A.
dependencies: MMseqs2 search and database utilities; temporary storage for two directional search results.
evidence: data/workflow/rbh.sh describes two directional searches, extracts best hits, swaps direction, merges/sorts and calls result2rbh; README lists RBH among supported modes.
limitations: No actual sequences or biological comparison are specified by this unit. Parameter asymmetry and ties/best-hit policy may affect results; interpretation as orthology requires evidence beyond RBH.

title: Iteratively expand sequence or profile search results
source_kind: shell workflow and documented CLI mode

sources.locator: initial target-profile search, profile creation and NUM_IT prefilter/alignment/expand/merge loop
Supported search modes > Iterative sequences-profile searches

scientific_use: Iteratively search sequence/profile targets, construct query profiles from hits and expand/merge aligned sequence results across iterations; useful for retrieving increasingly remote homolog candidates. README also documents iterative searches via num-iterations.
tool_role_basis: The inspected workflow orchestrates existing MMseqs2 search, result2profile, prefilter, align, expandaln and mergedbs operations.
inputs: Query sequence database, target profile database, underlying target sequence database, and target-profile alignment/results database; number of iterations and per-step search parameters.
outputs: Merged alignment result database containing results across iterations; temporary profiles and prefilter results.
dependencies: MMseqs2; precomputed profile database and its consensus/sequence/alignment artifacts; temporary storage. Profile preparation is upstream hidden state.
evidence: data/workflow/enrich.sh enforces the four upstream target/query databases and shows profile generation and iterative search/expansion/merge; README names iterative sequence-profile search.
limitations: The workflow is profile-target enrichment and assumes prepared target profile components; exact profile database construction and scoring choices were not inspected. No execution or biological validation.

title: Search nucleotide sequences in translated reading frames
source_kind: documented search modes and shell workflow

sources.locator: Supported search modes > Translated searches
QUERY_NUCL/TARGET_NUCL frame extraction and translation setup

scientific_use: Search nucleotide and protein sequence sets in translated combinations (README names blastx, tblastn and tblastx); the workflow can extract ORFs or frames and then search translated sequence databases. May support homology discovery when coding sequence is not directly represented as protein.
tool_role_basis: The workflow uses MMseqs2 frame/ORF extraction, translation and search/alignment modules; it applies existing algorithms.
inputs: Nucleotide and/or protein sequence database; selection of which side is nucleotide; ORF extraction versus frame extraction behavior.
outputs: Alignment/search result database with translated coordinates and sequence relationships, convertible to tabular alignment output.
dependencies: MMseqs2 and temporary storage; translation and frame extraction settings; correct nucleotide/protein orientation and coordinate interpretation.
evidence: README Supported search modes lists translated query/target combinations; data/workflow/translated_search.sh branches on QUERY_NUCL/TARGET_NUCL and invokes extractframes or extractorfs.
limitations: Only the setup portion of translated_search.sh was visible in the bounded source response; later result conversion and coordinate semantics remain open for inspection. No nucleotide dataset was identified.

title: Map highly similar nucleotide sequences with an ungapped-first search

kmersearch, optional rescorediagonal filtering, gapped alignment and nucleotide offset stages

tool_role_basis: The workflow composes existing MMseqs2 kmersearch, rescorediagonal, align, swapresults and offsetalignment commands.
inputs: Query and target sequence databases; optional nucleotide mode and ungapped filtering; similarity/search parameters.
outputs: Alignment result database, with nucleotide offsets restored when NUCL mode is selected.

evidence: README Supported search modes recommends mapping for very similar matches; data/workflow/linsearch.sh implements k-mer matching, optional ungapped filtering, local gapped alignment and nucleotide offset adjustment.

scientific_use: Reduce redundancy and cluster nucleotide sequences: first cluster redundancy, extract translated frames, prefilter/align, restore sequence coordinates and merge clusters. This is a distinct nucleotide-specific workflow from protein-sequence clustering.
tool_role_basis: This workflow composes MMseqs2 linclust, extractframes, prefilter, alignment, offsetalignment, clust and mergeclusters commands.
inputs: MMseqs2 nucleotide sequence database and selected prefilter/alignment/clustering parameters.
outputs: Merged cluster result database over original nucleotide input.
dependencies: MMseqs2 and intermediate storage; ORF/frame extraction and nucleotide coordinate restoration.

limitations: Implementation is a workflow source only; biological meaning of cluster criteria and resource suitability depends on the selected data and parameters. No execution was performed.

title: Summarize pairwise proteome alignment coverage

sources.locator: search, convertalis, parseproteomealignments and createtsv stages
parseproteomealignments function: source-ID aggregation, match counting and denominator by query proteome sequence count

scientific_use: Search proteins from one or more query proteomes against target proteomes, then aggregate the fraction of query-proteome entries with at least one alignment to each target proteome. The parser counts each target source at most once per query sequence and divides the count by the number of entries in that query proteome.
tool_role_basis: The workflow uses the existing MMseqs2 search and parser; parser implementation provides this proteome-level aggregation from alignments.
inputs: Query and target sequence databases retaining source/proteome grouping metadata; pairwise sequence search result database.
outputs: Per-query-source to target-source score table (fraction of query proteome entries with any alignment to a target proteome); also an alignment-format .m8 output.
dependencies: MMseqs2; source metadata in database lookup/source tables; memory allocation for a dense query-proteome by target-proteome score matrix.
evidence: easyproteomesearch.sh invokes search and parseproteomealignments then exports a TSV; parseproteomealignments.cpp increments each query-source/target-source cell once per query sequence and normalizes by query source entry count.
limitations: No proteome inputs are provided by inspected source. Dense score matrix grows with the product of query and target source counts; exact scientific interpretation depends on source grouping and alignment settings. Workflow output naming uses _score.tsv even though createtsv invocation includes RESULTS.tsv guard; output path behavior warrants a source follow-up.

title: Identify a pathogen from cerebrospinal-fluid metagenomic reads

sources.revision: mutable wiki; page reports edited 2026-09-07 and 29 revisions (retrieved 2026-09-30)
sources.locator: Metagenomic pathogen detection: The Patient, The Dataset, Assigning taxonomic labels, Investigating the pathogen

scientific_use: Translate CSF metagenomic nucleotide reads to putative protein fragments, search a curated protein reference with taxonomy labels, inspect LCA assignments/report, filter reads by candidate taxon, assemble pathogen reads to proteins with Plass, cluster assemblies and annotate representatives. Tutorial frames Powassan virus as the diagnostic mystery and asks readers to distinguish evidence from contamination/background and assess read-count significance.
tool_role_basis: The analysis uses MMseqs2 taxonomy, filtering and clustering tools and composes Plass assembly and web-based protein annotation; primarily tool use with workflow composition across packages.
inputs: Tutorial's filtered CSF sequencing read FASTA (reported 226,908 reads after human-read removal); UniProt Swiss-Prot snapshot uniprot_sprot_2018_03.fasta.gz plus mapping TSV; selected LCA settings; taxon ID for filtering; Plass and clustering inputs are derived from filtered reads.
outputs: Per-read LCA TSV and taxonomy report; taxon-filtered pathogen reads; assembled protein FASTA; representative sequence clusters for annotation.
dependencies: MMseqs2, Plass, SRA-related/download tools, FLASH for prepared paired-read merges, and MMseqs2 webserver target databases PFAM/PDB/Uniclust for the final annotation activity.
evidence: Tutorial sections state sample is CSF metagenomic sequencing, 14 million original reads with human reads removed and smaller 226,908-read SRA set; provide mystery_reads.fasta and Swiss-Prot 2018_03 downloads; show taxonomy, filtering, assembly, clustering commands and downstream questions; cited study is Piantadosi et al. 2018.
limitations: Wiki is mutable and no immutable wiki revision was resolved. It directs readers to general SRA documentation, not an accession for the filtered reads. Clinical diagnosis and biological truth are not established by source inspection; task grader must define contamination/background handling. Dataset terms and assembly/annotation were not checked or run.

title: Cluster a metagenomic protein catalogue from human-gut reads

sources.revision: mutable wiki; page reports edited 2026-09-07 and 29 revisions (retrieved 2026-09-30)
sources.locator: Writing large scale sequence analysis workflows > Analysis of a human gut metagenomics dataset > Getting a protein catalogue / Redundancy reduction

scientific_use: Use paired-end human-gut metagenomic reads to build a protein catalogue directly with Plass, compare catalogue yield against genomic assembly plus Prodigal protein prediction, then reduce catalogue redundancy with MMseqs2 easy-cluster/easy-linclust. Tutorial example uses 90% sequence identity and 95% member coverage and explains coverage modes and identity definition.
tool_role_basis: The analysis combines external Plass assembly and MEGAHIT/Prodigal comparison with MMseqs2 sequence clustering; its central clustering stage applies the existing MMseqs2 tool.
inputs: Paired-end FASTQ for SRA run ERR1384114 (ENA provides two paired files); resulting Plass protein catalogue or Prodigal-predicted proteins; chosen sequence identity and coverage settings.
outputs: Protein sequence catalogue; clustered representatives and cluster membership/all-sequences FASTA outputs; comparison of yield and redundancy.
dependencies: SRA Toolkit or ENA download, Plass, MMseqs2; MEGAHIT and Prodigal for comparison branch; large temporary storage and compute for metagenomic assembly/search.
evidence: Tutorial names human gut metagenomic SRA run ERR1384114 and ENA paired FASTQ URLs; directs Plass assembly directly from reads, contrasts MEGAHIT then Prodigal, and clusters with easy-cluster at --min-seq-id 0.9, -c 0.95, --cov-mode 1; lines 431-436 explain criteria.
limitations: Wiki is mutable; run size, study description, checksums and terms were not independently checked. Tutorial reports comparative performance claims without underlying benchmark outputs in this pass. This workflow is substantially more resource-intensive than the repository demonstration examples.
